bullets: Game 3 of 7 in the video (video 569.7s-733.7s, 164 s readable), vs Lava Hound beatdown: won, one crown up, after taking the enemy left tower at clock 1:36 - "That is most definitely tower down. What a beautiful predict" - and surviving the Hound counter-push with his own right tower at 584 HP.

The deck's plan against beatdown is stated outright: pressure the bridge in the windows where the opponent's cheap defence is spent. Battle Ram at the bridge at 2:48, Barbarian Barrel behind it at 2:35, Goblinstein in the back at 2:32 ("if he has lava then I can get a really nice spam push right now because he doesn't have the tombstone and cycle for my ebar"), Elite Barbarians at the bridge at 2:16.

When the Hound push arrives he does not try to out-defend it: at clock 1:32 he answers with Evo Elite Barbarians on the enemy King tower - "I can't really defend a pusher now. And just by doing this, I'm just forcing him to go in defensively" - and banks King-tower chip with Zap at 1:26 while cycling Mother Witch, Barbarian Barrel and Heal Spirit purely to avoid a three-crown.

Goblinstein is the deck's closer: pocketed at (8, 19) behind the enemy right tower at clock 0:56 and protected with Zap, Heal Spirit and Barbarian Barrel, then re-placed at 0:32 with an instant Lightning Link so it cannot be Fireballed - "if we insta ability, he can't fireball right away."
Cannon Cart, the eighth consensus slot, was never played in this game; the per-game HUD read instead showed Goblins and Tornado, which the match file treats as detection noise.

new_deck.rationale: Battle Ram and Elite Barbarians are dropped at the bridge on cycle to punish elixir windows, with Barbarian Barrel, Zap and Heal Spirit as cheap support rather than a control shell.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The deck answers a slow archetype by refusing to defend it. Ryley reads the opponent's cheap defence out of the equation (Tombstone spent, all elixir on a back-line Lava Hound) and puts Battle Ram and Evo Elite Barbarians at the bridge in exactly those windows, so the beatdown player has to spend on defence instead of building a push. Barbarian Barrel, Zap and Heal Spirit are one- and two-elixir top-ups that keep those pushes connecting, and Mother Witch doubles as swarm defence and as a threat the opponent must spell. Goblinstein is the heavy piece: safe in the back against spell-poor beatdown decks, then pocketed next to the enemy tower late with an instantly activated Lightning Link that denies the Fireball answer.
